thread:
alyssa: Heads-up — noticed a p99 regression on the hosted clusters around 02:30 UTC. Short seq tenants (<=64 tokens) are getting delayed when a handful of long sequences start KV rehydration. KV misses spike and then batching behavior seems to prefer long tails. attaching quick telemetry snippet.

jun: Ugh, seen similar. Do you have a flamegraph or kernel switch trace?

alyssa: Not a full flamegraph yet, but perf-bot ran the nightly profile. Key lines: 
```
perf-bot: profile summary (prod-run-02:30):
- kernel_switch_count +34% on cuda kernels during peak
- avg batch_size increased for long lanes from 6 -> 14
- KV cache miss latency 2.8x for tenants X,Y,Z (cold rehydrate)
- token-credit depletion on short-lane queue after 12s of long-burst
```

jun: That token-credit depletion is the smoking gun. Our current refill is batch-driven and biases by observed length; when long sequences flood, credits flow to them.

mike: Could the kernel selector be switching to a different matmul path for longer seqs causing latency non-linearity? We saw kernels with poor startup costs favored for big batches.

tara: I prototyped a tiny heuristic yesterday — "fairlock" — that reserves a minimum credit for short-lane tenants and caps continuous credit accrual to any single tenant for >2s. Config excerpt:
```
# fairlock config (toy)
{
  "min_credit_short_lane": 8,
  "max_continuous_credit_ms": 2000,
  "kv_prefill_window_ms": 500,
  "batch_formation": "kv-aware-priority"
}
```

alyssa: Nice. Also thinking about KV prefill: for tenant bursts with known long context we can pre-warm KV asynchronously to avoid rehydration stalls. Maybe tie prefill to kernel selection prediction.

perf-bot: small experiment results (A/B):
- baseline: p99 = 420ms
- fairlock + kv-prefill: p99 = 310ms (-26%)
- regression cases: p50 unchanged
Note: p99 improvement mostly for short-lane tenants during long-burst windows.

jun: That's promising. Two follow-ups: 1) need to ensure we don't hurt overall throughput on Dedicated (customers with committed capacity), 2) ensure the cap doesn't thrash kernel selection heuristics.

mike: For (1) we can make fairlock opt-in per-tenant (default off for Dedicated) and per-node for hosted. For (2) add a kernel-stability window — avoid switching matmul kernel inside a single request unless latency delta > 2x.

tara: I'll open a small PR with the heuristic gate and tests. Plan: staged rollout to canary nodes with telemetry flags: 
```
- ticket: eng-runtime#4521
- rollout: canary(4 nodes) -> region(2AZ) -> global
- telemetry: token-credit histograms, kernel-switch count, kv-miss latency
```

alyssa: Add a quick check to abort prefill if KV eviction pressure > 0.5 to avoid thrashing memory. Also add a debug log when fairlock kicks in: `fairlock:reserved=8 tenant=short-abc reason=kv-spike`.

perf-bot: scheduled nightly A/B with PR branch. Expecting ~12h to gather stable stats.

jun: If metrics hold, we should bake this into our batching heuristics — make it part of the token budget calculator rather than an ad-hoc gate. But incremental deploy looks good.

mike: FYI I'll instrument kernel selector to emit a small cost model delta so we can correlate kernel choice and observed p99 jump.

alyssa: Great. Thanks everyone. Tara, assign me the PR review and mark it high-priority for the canary window. I'll follow up with a short runbook for ops in case the fairlock causes regressions. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled for 1967013000.

tara: PR created: https://git.redwood.internal/r/eng-runtime/patches/314 (WIP). tagging jun/mike/alyssa for review.

alyssa: Closing loop — will post final numbers after the nightly. If p99 stays improved we can iterate on tighter budget targets and then promote to default for hosted free-tier.
